title: Arabic from A to Z
tagline: Learn to read first, then build the language one rule at a time, in the order the Madinah books teach it. Every lesson teaches before it tests.

stages.title: Stage 0 · Reading
stages.about: Letters, vowel marks and pronunciation, in the order of al-Qāʿida an-Nūrāniyya. After this stage you can sound out any fully voweled Arabic word.

lessons.title: The 28 letters
lessons.summary: Every letter's name and sound, learned in look-alike families.

lessons.title: How letters join
lessons.summary: Start, middle and end shapes, and the six letters that never join forward.

lessons.title: Short vowels
lessons.summary: Fatḥa, kasra and ḍamma: a, i, u.

lessons.title: Sukūn and shadda
lessons.summary: Stopping a letter, and doubling it.

lessons.title: Long vowels
lessons.summary: ا و ي stretch a vowel: ā, ū, ī.

lessons.title: Tanwīn and tāʾ marbūṭa
lessons.summary: The -un / -an / -in endings, and the feminine ة.

lessons.title: “The”: sun and moon letters
lessons.summary: Reading al- correctly, and the silent alif when words join.

stages.title: Stage 1 · The nominal sentence
stages.about: Follows the order of Madinah Book 1 (Durūs al-Lugha al-ʿArabiyya): pointing, asking, describing, owning, and the first verbs, ending with the three cases.

lessons.title: This is a book
lessons.summary: هَذَا and مَا: naming things around you.

lessons.title: Who is this?
lessons.summary: مَنْ for people, yes/no questions with أَ.

lessons.title: That
lessons.summary: Near and far, and joining with وَ.

lessons.title: The house is big
lessons.summary: “The” and your first full sentences: subject + description.

lessons.title: Where?
lessons.summary: فِي and عَلَى, and the kasra they cause.

lessons.title: Muhammad's book
lessons.summary: Possession by putting two nouns together (iḍāfa).

lessons.title: I, you, he, she
lessons.summary: Personal pronouns and “where are you from?”

lessons.title: This (feminine)
lessons.summary: Feminine nouns, ة, and هَذِهِ / تِلْكَ.

lessons.title: The big house
lessons.summary: Adjectives that follow and match their noun.

lessons.title: Calling someone, and family
lessons.summary: The vocative يَا and family words.

lessons.title: He went
lessons.summary: Your first verbs: the past tense and its doer.

lessons.title: The three cases
lessons.summary: Putting it together: rafʿ, naṣb, jarr, and words that never change.

method.title: How this course works
body: Teach, then practise, then test, always in that order. Each lesson has five steps: Learn the new words, Understand the rule (examples first, rule second, the inductive way an-Naḥw al-Wāḍiḥ teaches), Read a short passage, Practice with hints where mistakes don't count, then Check. Score 80% on the check and the next lesson unlocks.

Nothing is tested before it's taught. A script checks every passage and exercise before the site is published. If any Arabic word in a reading or quiz hasn't appeared in that lesson's teaching or an earlier one, the site won't deploy.

Reading before grammar. Stage 0 follows the order of al-Qāʿida an-Nūrāniyya, the primer used to teach Quran reading worldwide: letters, then joined forms, short vowels, sukūn and shadda, long vowels, tanwīn, then al-. Everything after it is fully voweled, so you never have to guess.

Grammar in the Madinah order. Stage 1 follows the sequence of Madinah Book 1 by Dr. V. ʿAbdur-Raḥīm, written for non-Arab students at the Islamic University of Madinah. Each lesson adds one structure on top of the last, and every rule appears inside real sentences. The text here is original, not copied from the books, so this course pairs well with them.

Spaced review. When you pass a lesson, its words join your review deck. They come back after 1, 3, 7, 16, 35 and 90 days, sooner if you miss them. Research on second-language vocabulary consistently finds that spaced retrieval beats re-reading for long-term memory.
Fuṣḥā first. This course teaches Modern Standard Arabic, the Arabic of the Quran's language family, books and news. A dialect can be added later on this foundation.
